harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to serve a chrooted web application on port 8080 as locked, unprivileged account appsvc. The systemd service starts at boot and recovered successfully after a verified node reboot. The installed RHEL release, kernel, SELinux enforcement, and existing Python runtime were preserved.
actions_performed: Created locked system account appsvc with /usr/sbin/nologin and no home directory.
Built a root-owned Python 3.12 chroot at /srv/app-chroot with read-only application code.
Installed and enabled app-chroot.service with restart and security hardening.
Opened TCP port 8080 persistently in firewalld.
Verified HTTP service, chroot confinement, UID/GID 992, zero active capabilities, protected files, and absence of an interactive session.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified changed boot identity and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Web application runs inside a chroot as appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: The Python process runs as appsvc, its process root is /srv/app-chroot, it listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, and both health and application requests succeed through the managed-node address.

evidence.requirement: Starts at boot without an interactive login session
evidence.summary: The service is enabled and active; appsvc has a locked password, nologin shell, and no interactive session. The current-boot journal proves automatic startup after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Security controls and persistent network access
evidence.summary: The live process has no permitted, effective, inherited, or ambient capabilities and has NoNewPrivileges enabled. Application/runtime files are not writable by appsvc, SELinux remains enforcing, and the runtime and permanent firewall rules allow only the requested port.

evidence.requirement: Compatible software with installed OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: The node remains RHEL 10.0 on kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 and uses its installed Python 3.12.9 runtime inside the chroot.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 6d37896c-e0cd-4fe7-acbf-94fc35781e09, received native reboot acknowledgement, observed new boot ID 0c40fc03-a79b-4d25-a0da-004a2aa8795e, and proved recovered service, application checksum, HTTP responses, firewall state, SELinux enforcement, and no failed units.
